cutScenes.reason: the offline queue page never left its loading state under the local fixture stack (getAllQueued() did not resolve), so the screen could not be shown honestly. Brief step 14 permits cutting scene 6 if sync fails. Attempted three times; evidence in capture/takes/.

qaRevision.note: Revised after the independent QA pass. Three narration claims were removed because the screens did not support them, s3's stored audio timing was corrected, and the closing line was added to the .srt.

voice.speedNote: MEASURED, not guessed. At 0.78 this voice read 145 words in 81.8s = 106 wpm, far under the brief's 140 wpm guidance. At 0.95 the same lines take 63.2s = ~138 wpm, which also lands inside the brief's '60 to 70 s of speech' window. The owner must confirm the pace by ear.

pronunciation.ISUFST: I S U F S T
pronunciation.IPOPHL: I P O P H L

voice.pronunciationNote: Applied to the text sent to synthesis only. Captions and the .srt keep the real spelling. Note that ISUFST expands to five spoken words, which is why scene 7 measures 10.9s for 19 written words. The owner confirms each name by ear.

captions.note: Captions carry explicit line breaks so the 40-character rule is checked per line, not on the whole string.

scenes.title: The problem

visual.photoCredit: JFVelasquez Floro, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
visual.subject: Garbage and plastic pollution in the Marilao River, Bulacan
visual.motion: slow push-in, 1.00 -> 1.08 scale, centred on the water
visual.why: Chosen for contrast: a wide shot with sky and riverbank, visually distinct from the detection photo in s3, which is a different frame of the same river.

scenes.caption:
Waste is reaching our rivers
every day.
scenes.narration: A citizen sees waste being dumped into a river. Who do they report it to — and will anyone ever answer?

scenes.title: One photo, Ghost Mode

visual.note: Real capture: open the camera, take the photo from the fake device (the staged photo), then turn Ghost Mode on.

scenes.caption:
One photo. Ghost Mode keeps
the reporter anonymous.
scenes.narration: With LikasLens, they take one photo. And when reporting feels risky, Ghost Mode keeps the reporter anonymous.

actions.why: turn Ghost Mode ON — the beat the narration describes
let the live camera stream settle so a viewer sees a camera, not a frozen frame
press the real capture control; the selector is resolved at record time

scenes.narrationNote: QA found the earlier line 'The location tags itself, automatically' was not demonstrated anywhere on screen: no address, map pin or 'location added' state appears in any frame. The claim was removed rather than the shot being faked.

scenes.title: The AI reads the photo

visual.note: C1: the AI Triage step shows the REAL triage response — real material labels — instead of the hardcoded simulation.

scenes.caption:
The AI flags what it
recognises. A person confirms.
scenes.narration: Our AI reads the photo and flags what it recognises in the scene. Nothing is final: a person confirms it before anything is acted on.
scenes.narrationNote: Deliberately does NOT name a material. The recorded take shows the labels 'Vehicle / Traffic' and 'e-waste' — naming 'plastic' here would describe something the screen did not show, which brief section 7 forbids.

actions.why: Ghost Mode on, as a real reporter would
capture; this is what kicks off the real triage call
the real triage call takes 10-20s on this machine, so the scene starts only once the result is on screen
the scene begins on the result, not on the spinner
hold on the result long enough to read

scenes.title: Liksi

visual.note: Open the Liksi chat bubble and send one question in English.

scenes.caption:
Liksi answers legal questions
in plain language.
scenes.narration: Liksi, the built-in assistant, answers questions about the law in plain language.

actions.value: What law covers plastic waste in a river?
actions.why: one question, one real Gemini answer
askLiksi already polls until the reply bubble appears, so the answer is on screen by now

scenes.title: The LGU side

visual.note: triage (Kanban) then lgu-performance. The tickets card grid is deliberately NOT used: every card renders ConfidenceTierBadge with showScore, which prints an AI confidence percentage — on the banned list.

scenes.caption:
Tracked tickets, response
times, and escalations.
scenes.narration: For local government, every report becomes a tracked ticket. Offices are measured on response time and SLA compliance, and escalations are counted.

actions.why: the board is empty until the ticket RPC answers
the LGU beat starts once the board actually has incidents on it
the page renders a Skeleton (animate-shimmer) until its data arrives; wait for real content, not the placeholder
start on the page that actually has data on it

scenes.narrationNote: QA found 'late ones show as escalations' and 'a public record shows how quickly they resolve' were not demonstrable. The wording now tracks the on-screen column headers RESPONSE, SLA and ESCALATED, and the AVG RESPONSE / SLA COMPLIANCE tiles.

timingCheck.note: Scene 6 was cut (see meta.cutScenes) and its 7s redistributed. Every scene still holds for its measured audio plus at least 0.4s. Narration is intentionally below the brief 60-70s speech guidance because cutting s6 removed 5.8s of speech without padding the remaining lines with claims the screen does not support.
